```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)
library(broom)

members_raw <- read_csv("~/Desktop/STA130 Final Project/rstudio-export/Member_Background.csv")
services_raw <- read_csv("~/Desktop/STA130 Final Project/rstudio-export/Service_Deliveries.csv")
purple <- "#5945A8"
lavender <- "#B9A9DC"
coral <- "#D66F7C"
blue <- "#589ABF"
plot_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom")

# Month-level registration dates: March 2024 is classified before
members <- members_raw %>%
  mutate(registration_date = make_date(member_start_year, member_start_month, 1))
services <- services_raw %>%
  mutate(event_date = make_date(delivery_year, delivery_month, delivery_day))

# RQ1: A member attended if there is at least one Present event from
# registration day through day 30 (inclusive).
registration <- members %>%
  filter(!is.na(registration_date)) %>%
  left_join(services, by = "member_id") %>%
  mutate(days_since = as.numeric(event_date - registration_date)) %>%
  group_by(member_id, registration_date) %>%
  summarise(
    has_records = any(!is.na(event_date)),
    attended_30 = any(attendance_status == "Present" &
                        days_since >= 0 & days_since <= 30, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    attended_status = case_when(
      !has_records ~ "No Data",
      attended_30 ~ "Attended",
      TRUE ~ "Did Not Attend"
    ),
    implementation_group = factor(
      if_else(registration_date < ymd("2024-03-04"), "Before", "After"),
      levels = c("Before", "After")
    )
  )

rq1_valid <- registration %>% filter(attended_status != "No Data")
rq1_counts <- rq1_valid %>%
  count(implementation_group, attended_status, name = "n") %>%
  complete(implementation_group,
           attended_status = c("Attended", "Did Not Attend"),
           fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(implementation_group) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(n), share = n / total) %>%
  ungroup()

rq1_all <- registration %>%
  count(implementation_group, attended_status, name = "n") %>%
  complete(implementation_group,
           attended_status = c("Attended", "Did Not Attend", "No Data"),
           fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(implementation_group) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(n), share = n / total) %>%
  ungroup()

attended_n <- rq1_counts %>% filter(attended_status == "Attended") %>% arrange(implementation_group)
# prop.test reports an asymptotic confidence interval for before-minus-after.
rq1_test <- prop.test(x = attended_n$n, n = attended_n$total, correct = FALSE)
rq1_before <- attended_n$share[1]
rq1_after <- attended_n$share[2]
rq1_gap <- 100 * (rq1_before - rq1_after)
rq1_no_data <- rq1_all %>%
  filter(attended_status == "No Data") %>%
  arrange(implementation_group) %>% pull(share)

# RQ2 and RQ3: attendance among recorded service registrations.
member_rates <- members %>%
  left_join(services, by = "member_id") %>%
  group_by(member_id) %>%
  summarise(
    age_years = first(age_years),
    types_of_cancer = first(types_of_cancer),
    total_events = sum(!is.na(attendance_status)),
    attended_events = sum(attendance_status == "Present", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(total_events > 0) %>%
  mutate(attendance_rate = 100 * attended_events / total_events)

age_missing <- sum(is.na(member_rates$age_years))
age_zero <- sum(member_rates$age_years == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
age_data <- member_rates %>% filter(!is.na(age_years), age_years > 0, age_years <= 120)
age_model <- lm(attendance_rate ~ age_years, data = age_data)
age_coef <- tidy(age_model) %>% filter(term == "age_years")
age_r2 <- glance(age_model)$r.squared

# Cancer types can be multiple per member; membership is not exclusive.
members_long <- member_rates %>%
  mutate(types_of_cancer = strsplit(as.character(types_of_cancer), ";")) %>%
  unnest(types_of_cancer) %>%
  mutate(types_of_cancer = trimws(types_of_cancer)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(types_of_cancer), types_of_cancer != "", types_of_cancer != "Other")
cancer_counts <- members_long %>% count(types_of_cancer, sort = TRUE)
top_two <- head(cancer_counts, 2)$types_of_cancer
bottom_two <- tail(cancer_counts, 2)$types_of_cancer
cancer_data <- members_long %>%
  filter(types_of_cancer %in% c(top_two, bottom_two)) %>%
  mutate(
    category = if_else(types_of_cancer %in% top_two, "Most prevalent", "Least prevalent"),
    types_of_cancer = factor(types_of_cancer, levels = c(top_two, bottom_two))
  )
cancer_summary <- cancer_data %>%
  group_by(types_of_cancer, category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(attendance_rate), median = median(attendance_rate),
            .groups = "drop")

# Exact p value generated from the supplied data (not read from a screenshot).
# For ties, base R will use an asymptotic approximation.
cancer_test <- wilcox.test(attendance_rate ~ category, data = cancer_data,
                          exact = FALSE)
rare_n <- sum(cancer_summary$n[cancer_summary$category == "Least prevalent"])

fmt_pct <- function(x, digits = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, digits = digits, format = "f"), "%")
fmt_p <- function(x) if (x < .001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("%.3f", x)
```

## Executive summary

::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Registration system**

**`r fmt_pct(rq1_before)` → `r fmt_pct(rq1_after)`**

First-month attendance was lower after implementation, among members with records.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Age**

**`r sprintf("%.2f", age_coef$estimate)` points / year**

Age explains only **`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * age_r2)`%** of attendance variation.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Cancer type**

**Wilcoxon p = `r fmt_p(cancer_test$p.value)`**

Pooled comparison: `r if (cancer_test$p.value < .05) "statistically significant" else "not statistically significant"`; the rare groups are small.
:::
:::

**Priority:** Improve the completeness and comparability of registration and attendance records before drawing causal conclusions or targeting outreach by demographics.

## Context and data: Measuring member participation

**Wellspring** provides support programs and services for people affected by cancer. It introduced a new registration system on **March 4, 2024** and expanded online programming.

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Questions**

1. Did first-month attendance differ before versus after implementation?
2. Does age predict attendance rate?
3. Do the most and least prevalent cancer types have different attendance rates?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Data used**

- Member file: member ID, age, cancer type, registration month
- Service file: member ID, event date, attendance status
- Service attendance rate = Present events ÷ recorded events
:::
:::

*Observational analysis: the results describe associations, not the causal impact of the system.*

## RQ1: First-month attendance was lower after implementation

**Question:** Did the share attending at least one event within 30 days differ across implementation groups?

**Method:** Two-sample proportion test; members with **No Data excluded** from the primary comparison.

::: columns
::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r rq1_chart, fig.width=5.6, fig.height=3.2}
rq1_counts %>%
  mutate(attended_status = factor(attended_status, levels = c("Attended", "Did Not Attend"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(implementation_group, share, fill = attended_status)) +
  geom_col(width = .58) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(share * 100), "% (n=", n, ")")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = .5), size = 3.0) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Attended" = purple, "Did Not Attend" = lavender)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Members (%)", fill = "Attendance", subtitle = "Excluding 'No Data'") +
  plot_theme
```
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
**Before:** `r fmt_pct(rq1_before)` attended

**After:** `r fmt_pct(rq1_after)` attended

**Difference:** `r sprintf("%.1f", rq1_gap)` percentage points

95% CI: `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rq1_test$conf.int[1])` to `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rq1_test$conf.int[2])` points

$\chi^2$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", unname(rq1_test$statistic))`; p `r fmt_p(rq1_test$p.value)`
:::
:::

## RQ1: Missing records complicate the before/after comparison

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r rq1_missing_chart, fig.width=6.1, fig.height=3.4}
rq1_all %>%
  mutate(attended_status = factor(attended_status,
           levels = c("Attended", "Did Not Attend", "No Data"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(implementation_group, share, fill = attended_status)) +
  geom_col(width = .58) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(share >= .065, paste0(round(share * 100), "%"), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = .5), size = 3.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Attended" = purple,
                               "Did Not Attend" = lavender, "No Data" = coral)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Members (%)", fill = "Attendance", subtitle = "Including 'No Data'") +
  plot_theme
```
:::
::: {.column width="43%"}
**No Data:** `r fmt_pct(rq1_no_data[1])` before versus `r fmt_pct(rq1_no_data[2])` after.

- After-period members have shorter potential follow-up.
- Missing or delayed service records may affect the comparison.
- Dates are **month-level**; everyone registered in March 2024 is counted as **Before**.

**Interpretation:** The observed decline does **not** establish that the new system caused it.
:::
:::

## RQ2: Age is statistically associated with attendance, but weakly

**Method:** Member-level linear regression of service attendance rate (%) on age (years).

::: columns
::: {.column width="59%"}
```{r age_chart, fig.width=6.3, fig.height=3.6}
ggplot(age_data, aes(age_years, attendance_rate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .28, size = .9, color = blue) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = coral, linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Attendance rate (%)") +
  plot_theme
```
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**Each additional year:** `r sprintf("%+.2f", age_coef$estimate)` percentage points (p = `r fmt_p(age_coef$p.value)`).

**10 years:** `r sprintf("%+.1f", 10 * age_coef$estimate)` points.

**$R^2$:** `r sprintf("%.4f", age_r2)` (about `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * age_r2)`% of variation).

**Sample:** `r nrow(age_data)` of `r nrow(member_rates)` members with service records.

Missing age: `r age_missing`; age 0: `r age_zero`.
:::
:::

*Age alone is too weak a predictor to justify age-based outreach.*

## RQ3: Cancer-type differences need cautious interpretation

**Method:** Compare two most versus two least prevalent types using member attendance rates; Wilcoxon rank-sum test on pooled groups.

::: columns
::: {.column width="53%"}
```{r cancer_chart, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
ggplot(cancer_data, aes(types_of_cancer, attendance_rate, fill = category)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = .45, width = .58) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Most prevalent" = blue, "Least prevalent" = coral)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attendance rate (%)", fill = "Group") +
  coord_flip() + plot_theme
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r cancer_table, results='asis'}
library(knitr)

cancer_summary |>
  mutate(
    `Cancer type` = case_when(
      types_of_cancer == "Gallbladder and Bile Duct" ~
        "Gallbladder/Bile Duct",
      TRUE ~ as.character(types_of_cancer)
    ),
    Mean = sprintf("%.1f%%", mean),
    Median = sprintf("%.1f%%", median)
  ) |>
  select(`Cancer type`, n, Mean, Median) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'style="font-size: 14px; width: 95%; table-layout: auto;"'
  )
```

**Wilcoxon p = `r fmt_p(cancer_test$p.value)`** — `r if (cancer_test$p.value < .05) "statistically significant at 5%; interpret carefully" else "not significant at 5%"`.

Least-prevalent groups: **`r rare_n` observations combined**.
:::
:::

*Differences in sample means are descriptive; they do not establish significant pairwise differences.*

## Limitations

1. **Month level dates.** Registration days are unavailable. March 2024 registrations are all classified Before, although the change happened March 4.

2. **Missing and unequal follow-up.** No Data is more common in the After group, which also has less time for attendance to be observed.

3. **Incomplete age records.** `r age_missing` of `r nrow(member_rates)` members with recorded services lack age (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * age_missing/nrow(member_rates))`%); `r age_zero` have age 0.

4. **Small cancer subgroups and observational design.** Only `r rare_n` observations are in the two least prevalent groups; unmeasured differences may affect every comparison.

## Recommendations: Improve evidence before targeting outreach

**1 Highest priority — Audit registration and service records.**

Investigate missing attendance statuses, delayed entries, and whether post-implementation members have adequate follow-up. Preserve exact registration dates where possible.

**2 Next — Monitor comparable cohorts.**

Track a consistent 30-day attendance outcome only after each new member has had enough follow-up. Repeat the before/after analysis once the data are more complete.

**3 Then — Investigate participation barriers.**

Explore scheduling, accessibility, program preferences, and reminder processes. Do not target by age alone or infer rare-cancer needs from tiny samples.

## Conclusion

- **Registration:** First-month attendance differs before versus after implementation, but missing records and unequal observation windows prevent a causal claim.

- **Age:** A statistically detectable positive relationship has very little explanatory power in practice.

- **Cancer type:** Results are descriptive and `r if (cancer_test$p.value < .05) "the pooled test is statistically significant, though sample imbalance limits interpretation" else "the pooled Wilcoxon test does not show a statistically significant difference"`; rare groups cannot support strong recommendations.

**Takeaway:** Better tracking is the most actionable immediate step for Wellspring.

## Appendix: Definitions, exclusions, and statistical checks

- **RQ1 outcome:** Attended at least one event marked `Present` during days 0–30 after the approximated registration date. Main comparison excludes `No Data` (no dated service record).
- **Implementation groups:** Before = registration date earlier than March 4, 2024. Dates use the **first day of each recorded month**, therefore March is Before.
- **RQ2/RQ3 attendance rate:** `100 × (# events marked Present / # recorded attendance statuses)` per member; excludes members with no service attendance statuses.
- **Age regression:** Ages missing, 0, or over 120 are excluded.
- **RQ3 categories:** Split semicolon-separated cancer types; exclude blank/Other; most/least prevalent chosen by counts among members with service records. Members with more than one type may appear multiple times.
- **Tests:** Two-sample proportion test (RQ1), OLS regression (RQ2), pooled Wilcoxon rank-sum test (RQ3). All statistics are computed when this file renders.
